questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Without changing the direction of the axes, the origin is transferred to the point (2,3). Then the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x-6 y+9=0$ changes to
questions.solution:
Put 
$x=x^{\prime}+2$ and $\quad y=y^{\prime}+3\therefore \quad x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x-6 y+9=0$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \quad $\left(x^{\prime}+2\right)^{2}$+$\left(y^{\prime}+3\right)^{2}-4 \left(x^{\prime}+2\right) \\
-6(y+3)+9=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+4+4 x^{2}+y^{2}+9 \\
\quad+6 y^{\prime}-4 x^{2}-8-6 y^{\prime}-18+9=0 \\
\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-4=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+y^{2}=4
\end{array} $

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The least value of $2 x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x y+2 x-3 y+8$ for real numbers $x$ and $y,$ is
questions.solution: $2 x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x y+2 x-3 y+8=\frac{1}{2}\left|4 x^{2}+2 y^{2}+4 x y+4 x-6 y+16\right|=\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(y^{2}-8 y\right)+\left(4 x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x y+4 x+2 y\right)+16\right].=\frac{1}{2}\left|(y-4)^{2}+(2 x+y+1)^{2}-1\right|$ So, least value will be $-\frac{1}{2}$ at $y=4$ and $x=\frac{-5}{2}$
